events.title: Visual Studio Code 1.142: Quickly identify the active harness
events.summary: Chat titles show the active harness name, such as Copilot or Codex, so you can identify it without opening the harness picker or hovering over the session list.

events.title: Visual Studio Code 1.142: Stop background shells
events.summary: In Copilot harness sessions, the background shells pill above the chat input lists the commands that the agent is still running in the background. When one of those commands is no longer useful, for example a test run that you want to restart or a command that runs longer than expected, you can stop it instead of waiting for it to finish. events.title: Visual Studio Code 1.142: Stateful responses for BYOK custom endpoints
events.summary: If your bring-your-own-key (BYOK) model uses a stateless Responses API, set "statefulResponses": false on its model entry in chatLanguageModels.json to send full conversation history with each request. See Custom Endpoint configuration for details.
events.sectionTitle: Stateful responses for BYOK custom endpoints

events.title: Visual Studio Code 1.141: Arrange sessions in a grid
events.summary: Compare results, monitor long-running tasks, or work across related conversations without repeatedly switching between sessions. Like in the editor window, the two-dimensional session grid in the Agents window lets you drag sessions into horizontal or vertical splits and resize the panes. Maximize a session when you need to focus, then return to the grid to continue working across conversations.

events.summary: Nested sessions let you split related work across separate conversations. events.title: Visual Studio Code 1.139: Rename sessions and chats in place
events.summary: Rename a session or nested chat directly in the sessions list. Double-click its title, use the Rename context menu action, or focus the row and press F2 for a session or F2 for a nested chat. Inline validation prevents blank titles, and canceling restores the previous title.

events.summary: Thank you to everyone who submitted a name for the VS Code pet. The naming contest closed on September 17, 2026, and we're reviewing the eligible entries. events.summary: The Claude and Codex agents in the Agents window rely on an SDK that is not shipped with VS Code and is downloaded when you first need it.
